speaker: Unknown
en: They're all trying to figure out, either for trophy reasons or for economic reasons, how do I break into something?
zh: 他们都在试图弄清楚,无论是为了炫耀还是为了经济利益,我如何入侵某个东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: So it requires us all to be very innovative.
zh: 所以这要求我们所有人都非常有创新性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every new technology that comes to the market requires a different kind of sort of harnesses, different kind of tools, different kind of capabilities in our products.
zh: 每一项进入市场的新技术都需要不同类型的驾驭方式、不同类型的工具、我们产品中不同类型的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you don't pay attention to every new technology, the customers start buying something else.
zh: 如果你没有关注每一项新技术,客户就开始去买别的东西了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's almost like we have to stay on our toes on a constant basis to anticipate technologies and to anticipate bad actors makes us the most innovative companies, the most innovative sector.
zh: 这几乎就像我们必须时刻保持警惕,去预判技术、预判坏人,这使我们成为最具创新性的公司、最具创新性的行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: In that environment, it's impossible that all the innovation is going to come from us, right?
zh: 在这种环境下,所有的创新不可能都来自我们,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because there's always somebody else who's got a different angle.
zh: 因为总会有别人从不同的角度看问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's always somebody else who's tried something that's going to work better than what I thought about.
zh: 总会有别人尝试过某些东西，效果比我想到的更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you just have to...
zh: 所以你只需要……

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to live in this industry with humility to understand that you may not always have all the answers.
zh: 你必须带着谦卑活在这个行业里，明白你可能并不总是拥有所有答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: The question is, however, are you smart enough to anticipate who has the answers, make them part of your team, charm them, be part of PowerAuto, and when we do that, can you then deploy that as quickly as you can to your customers?
zh: 但问题是，你是否足够聪明，能预判谁有答案，让他们成为你团队的一部分，打动他们，成为 PowerAuto 的一员，而当我们做到这些时，你能否尽快把它部署给你的客户？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think in the last eight years it's fair to say we've struck the right balance between what we build internally.
zh: 所以我认为，过去八年，公平地说，我们在内部构建的东西之间取得了恰当的平衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we can go rapidly and build internally and layer on top of our platforms and what is unique out of the market where if we partner slash acquire somebody, how can we bring them into the fullest part of Palo Alto and deploy the capability of our customer as quickly as we can.
zh: 包括我们能快速在内部构建并叠加到我们平台之上的东西，以及市场上独特的东西——如果我们合作或收购某人，如何把他们带进 Palo Alto 最核心的部分，并尽快把这种能力部署给我们的客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: The North Star always is, how do I deliver that capability to my customer as quickly as I can?
zh: 北极星始终是：我如何能尽快把这种能力交付给我的客户？

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes it's buy, sometimes it's build because it's too complicated to buy and integrate.
zh: 有时是买，有时是自建，因为买下来再整合太复杂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes we look at it and say, you know, it's not worth it.
zh: 有时我们看了看会说，你知道，这不值得。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let somebody else serve that part of the market.
zh: 让别人去服务那部分市场吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can find a way to integrate with them.
zh: 我们可以找到与他们整合的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So once you do make an acquisition, what is the playbook for getting them to your customers?
zh: 那么一旦你真的完成了一次收购，把他们带到你的客户面前的打法是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you onboard them, one, on the product basis, but then also on the team?
zh: 你如何让他们上手，一方面是在产品层面，另一方面是在团队层面？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, you know, we've done acquisitions of all shapes and sizes.
zh: 嗯，你知道，我们做过各种规模各种形式的收购。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of them have been easier because they're clear product acquisitions and categories we don't play in.
zh: 其中一些更容易，因为它们是明确的产品收购，而且是我们没有涉足的品类。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that becomes a lot easier because then we, all we do is we say, listen, you're going to be part of Palo Alto.
zh: 所以这就变得容易得多，因为那样，我们要做的就是：听着，你将成为 Palo Alto 的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: We might slow you down, but we're going to throw more resources at you so we can make you get more scale and more speed.
zh: 我们可能会拖慢你，但我们会向你投入更多资源，这样我们就能让你获得更大的规模和更快的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's kind of worked well with our browser company.
zh: 这在我们的浏览器公司身上效果不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't have to, we had to integrate in part of our product, but we were able to let them lose.
zh: 我们不必——我们必须整合进我们产品的一部分，但我们能够放他们放手去干。

speaker: Unknown
en: We bought a bunch of AI security capability, again, something we didn't do.
zh: 我们买了一堆 AI 安全能力，同样，这是我们之前没做过的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had to put more resources in there, put it together and let them lose.
zh: 我们投入了更多资源，把它们整合起来，然后放他们放手去干。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now what letting them lose means is we actually make them part of our go-to-market engine.
zh: 现在放他们放手去干意味着，我们实际上让他们成为我们市场推广引擎的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our teams out in the field have tons of relationships.
zh: 我们在外面的团队拥有大量关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are used to talking to their customers about unique things that we do.
zh: 他们习惯于与客户谈论我们做的独特的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: In that context, we sort of plug these capabilities into our go-to-market pipeline.
zh: 在这种背景下，我们把这些能力接入我们的市场推广管道。

speaker: Unknown
en: We make sure our customers are aware of the capabilities.
zh: 我们确保我们的客户了解这些能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: That allows our customers to go out there and use these capabilities as fast as we can give it to them.
zh: 这让我们的客户能够以我们交付的最快速度去使用这些能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think the biggest mistakes are that people make during the acquisition?
zh: 你认为人们在收购过程中犯的最大错误是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The biggest mistake that people make during acquisitions is underestimate the intelligence of the people who built the business that you acquired.
zh: 人们在收购过程中犯的最大错误是低估了被收购业务的打造者的智慧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because sometimes you take on the imperialistic attitude, I bought you, hence you must work for me.
zh: 因为有时你会采取一种帝国主义态度：我买下了你，所以你必须为我工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our attitude is, you kicked our ass, come tell us what you did wrong, come run this for us because you did well without our money, our resources, our scale, so you must have figured something out.
zh: 我们的态度是，你把我们打得落花流水，来告诉我们你做对了什么，来替我们运营这个业务，因为在没有我们的资金、我们的资源、我们的规模的情况下你都做得这么好，所以你一定悟出了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we spend our time trying to understand what they figured out.
zh: 所以我们花时间试图理解他们悟出了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Find a way that we can make that part of our culture, make that, absorb that capability, and we let them run it.
zh: 找到办法让它成为我们文化的一部分，吸收那种能力，然后我们让他们来运营。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that sometimes really makes it hard for my teams because they suddenly have a new boss in a category where they thought we were acquiring something.
zh: 而这有时真的让我的团队很难受，因为他们突然在一个品类里有了新老板，而他们原以为我们是去收购什么东西的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's just as I said, you have to approach this as humility because there are people out there who are smarter, faster, better resources, more resourceful than you in certain categories.
zh: 但就像我说的，你必须以谦卑来对待这件事，因为在某些品类里，总有人比你更聪明、更快、资源更好、更足智多谋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you can embrace them in the right way, it allows us to build a durable business.
zh: 而如果你能以正确的方式接纳他们，这能让我们打造出基业长青的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: This episode is brought to you by Brex, my favorite.
zh: 本集节目由 Brex 呈现，我的最爱。

speaker: Unknown
en: You become what you spend on, and I refuse to spend my time on work that shouldn't exist.
zh: 你花什么钱，就成什么样的人，而我拒绝把时间花在不该存在的工作上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Expense reports, receipt chasing, and manual closes.
zh: 报销单、追发票、手工结账。

speaker: Unknown
en: The companies building what's next from Vercel, OpenAI, Anthropic, Granola, and Deepgram all made the same call.
zh: 打造未来的那些公司——Vercel、OpenAI、Anthropic、Granola 和 Deepgram——都做了同样的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: They all run on Brex.
zh: 它们都运行在 Brex 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Brex is the intelligent finance platform that combines cards, expenses, and banking into a single stack.
zh: Brex 是智能金融平台，把卡片、报销和银行业务整合成一个体系。

speaker: Unknown
en: With agentic finance built in.
zh: 内置智能体金融。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI agents that handle expenses automatically, enforce policy before spend happens, and close your books in minutes.
zh: 处理报销的智能体 AI、在支出发生之前执行政策、几分钟内完成结账。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why Sorcery runs on Brex, so I can spend time on building and not busy work.
zh: 这就是为什么 Sorcery 运行在 Brex 上，这样我就可以把时间花在构建上，而不是琐事上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's time to get Brex AF.
zh: 是时候让 Brex AF 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn more at brex.com slash sorcery.
zh: 到 brex.com/sorcery 了解更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's b-r-e-x dot com slash s-o-u-r-c-e-r-y.
zh: 网址是 b-r-e-x 点 com 斜杠 s-o-u-r-c-e-r-y。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bye.
zh: 再见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Turing is training the next generation of AI with tasks that require real expertise and real-world judgment.
zh: Turing 正在用需要真正专业知识和真实世界判断力的任务训练下一代 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why companies like NVIDIA, Anthropic, Salesforce, and Gemini partner with Turing.
zh: 这就是为什么像 NVIDIA、Anthropic、Salesforce 和 Gemini 这样的公司与 Turing 合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Turing builds realistic reinforcement learning environments and data systems based on real operational traces, the kind of infrastructure Frontier Labs need to train superintelligence.
zh: Turing 基于真实运营轨迹构建逼真的强化学习环境和数据系统，这正是 Frontier Labs 训练超级智能所需的那种基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit Turing.com slash S-O-U-R-C-E-R-Y.
zh: 访问 Turing.com/sourcery。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you remain curious in this exploration process of finding new potential acquisitions, new companies to bring in?
zh: 在寻找潜在收购对象、寻找新公司的探索过程中，你如何保持好奇心？

speaker: Unknown
en: Paranoia.
zh: 偏执。

speaker: Unknown
en: Paranoia?
zh: 偏执？

speaker: Unknown
en: Fear of failure.
zh: 对失败的恐惧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Remember in the fear-mongering business?
zh: 记得我们是在贩卖恐惧的行业里吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I also live with the fear of failure.
zh: 我自己也活在对失败的恐惧中。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's this constant idea that imagine that something happens out there and there is no security solution.
zh: 就是这种挥之不去的念头：想象一下外面发生了什么，而没有任何安全解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And today, we're deluged with people like you doing these podcasts with these cool CEOs who are building all kinds of new tech.
zh: 而今天，我们被像你这样的人淹没，做着这些播客，访谈这些正在构建各种新技术的酷炫 CEO 们。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can barely understand half of them.
zh: 他们说的一半你几乎都听不懂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, we're going to do open-weight models versus closed-weight models.
zh: 哦，我们要搞开放权重模型对战闭源权重模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, how do I figure out what an open-weight model is?
zh: 那么，我怎么弄明白开放权重模型是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, now you've got an open-weight model.
zh: 好了，现在你有了开放权重模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the consequences from a security perspective?
zh: 从安全角度看，后果是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Does it change the game?
zh: 它会改变游戏规则吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you do with agents?
zh: 你要怎么处理智能体？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, shit, we've got agents now.
zh: 哦，见鬼，现在我们有智能体了。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we deal with security with agents?
zh: 我们该怎么处理智能体安全问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do I find one in the first place?
zh: 首先，我怎么找到它们？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, they're going to be all over the place.
zh: 嗯，它们将无处不在。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we start thinking about them and bring a bunch of people together and say, dude, these things called agents, where are they going to be?
zh: 于是我们开始思考它们，把一群人聚在一起说，伙计，这些叫智能体的东西，它们会出现在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, they're going to be everywhere.
zh: 嗯，它们会无处不在。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're going to be in SaaS software.
zh: 它们会出现在 SaaS 软件里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our infrastructure is going to be on-prem.
zh: 我们的基础设施会在本地部署。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we collect them together?
zh: 我们怎么把它们汇集起来？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've got to figure this out.
zh: 我们得把这件事搞清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we then start looking at the marketing.
zh: 于是我们开始看市场上的动向。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is anybody working on this problem?
zh: 有人在做这个问题吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: How are we thinking about it?
zh: 我们对它怎么看？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's where we find out, oh, these guys are thinking about it the same way we are.
zh: 就是在那里我们发现，哦，这些家伙在用和我们一样的方式思考这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: They started thinking about it one year ago.
zh: 他们一年前就开始思考了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's cool.
zh: 那挺好。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do we do?
zh: 我们该做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Should we build it?
zh: 我们该自己造吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because they're thinking about it the same way, or should we acquire them?
zh: 因为他们和我们的思考方式一样，还是该收购他们？

speaker: Unknown
en: You talk to them saying, do you want to come?
zh: 你去跟他们谈，说，你想来我们这儿吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, no, we're going to be so big, we don't need you.
zh: 他们会说，不用了，我们会做得很大，不需要你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then you can move on.
zh: 那你就可以继续往前走了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a whole sort of discovery process of what is the technology?
zh: 所以这整个是一种发现过程：这项技术是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the implications of security?
zh: 它对安全意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you solve the security problem?
zh: 你怎么解决这个安全问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about it?
zh: 你怎么看这个问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where does it fit in our portfolio?
zh: 它在我们产品组合中处于什么位置？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it going to be big?
zh: 它会做大吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: If so, should we build it?
zh: 如果会，我们该自己造吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we build it?
zh: 我们能造出来吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we late?
zh: 我们是不是太晚了？

speaker: Unknown
en: Should we also at the same time look at what's happening in the market, which we do, and then decide, well, it's probably better to build it because it's going to be more complicated to buy that integrated, or it's just better to buy something because it's a lot easier for us to go run with it because they're ahead.
zh: 我们是不是也应该同时看看市场上正在发生什么——我们也确实这么做——然后再决定：自己造可能更好，因为买那种集成的东西会更复杂；或者直接买现成的更好，因为对方领先，我们直接拿来跑会容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hamza mentioned when we were over there that you do see things many years before, like you're very good at predicting things like the Sasspocalypse.
zh: Hamza 提到，我们在那边的时候，你说你常常提前很多年就能看到一些事情，比如你很擅长预测像 Sasspocalypse 这样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, actually, I didn't predict the Sasspocalypse.
zh: 其实，Sasspocalypse 并不是我预测的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought you did.
zh: 我以为是你预测的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I predict the end of the Sasspocalypse as opposed to the beginning of it.
zh: 我预测的是 Sasspocalypse 的结束，而不是它的开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the market got ahead of itself.
zh: 我认为市场走得太前面了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think when AI came out, I think people started trying to predict what's going to happen to the AI.
zh: 我认为 AI 出现的时候，人们开始试图预测 AI 会带来什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there was this notion that AI is going to eat software.
zh: 当时有一种说法是 AI 会吞噬软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the market indiscriminately decided that every software company was destined to zero.
zh: 市场不加区分地断定每一家软件公司都注定归零。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you saw the entire SaaS market went down 50%.
zh: 于是你看到整个 SaaS 市场跌了 50%。

speaker: Unknown
en: You sat there and say, this makes no sense.
zh: 你坐在那里会说，这毫无道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI can be great at finding vulnerabilities.
zh: AI 可以很擅长发现漏洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI can be great at 80% use cases.
zh: AI 可以很好地搞定 80% 的使用场景。

speaker: Unknown
en: We live in the 0.1% use case.
zh: 而我们生活在 0.1% 的用例里。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're looking for the needle in the haystack.
zh: 我们要找的是干草堆里的针。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is not good at looking for every needle in the haystack.
zh: AI 并不擅长在干草堆里找每一根针。

speaker: Unknown
en: We write machine learning code.
zh: 我们写机器学习代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: We look for a whole bunch of attack techniques.
zh: 我们寻找一大堆攻击手法。

speaker: Unknown
en: We find the 0.1% use case just the way somebody goes and tells the car where to turn.
zh: 我们找到那 0.1% 的用例，就像有人告诉汽车该往哪转弯一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a tree.
zh: 那是一棵树。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's the edge case.
zh: 那是边界情况（edge case）。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI doesn't understand every edge case.
zh: AI 并不理解每一个边界情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: It does the mainstream cases.
zh: 它处理的是主流情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we declared the Sasecalypse for cybersecurity was over.
zh: 所以我们宣告，针对网络安全的 Sasecalypse 已经结束了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We did not believe that we were going to get impacted.
zh: 我们不相信我们会受到冲击。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can see now that was six months ago.
zh: 而现在你可以看到，那是六个月前的事了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We seem to be having a moment.
zh: 我们似乎正迎来属于我们的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think, though, about the broader macro market?
zh: 不过，你怎么看更宏观的市场？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think that some of these companies will actually not recover?
zh: 你觉得这些公司里会不会有一些实际上再也恢复不了了？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you mean?
zh: 你指的是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of these companies are down like 90% and still haven't.
zh: 其中一些公司跌了 90% 到现在还没恢复。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, that's a fair question.
zh: 你看，这是个合理的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think every company is different.
zh: 我认为每家公司都不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every company is different in terms of what the capability they bring to the market or the market believes that either that capability is going to be par for the course.
zh: 每家公司都不一样，在于它们带给市场的能力是什么，或者市场认为这种能力是会成为常态。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think there's a lot of questions in terms of what the native capability of AI models is going to be.
zh: 所以我认为，关于 AI 模型的原生能力会是什么样，有很多疑问。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if that native capability is exposed to me, you as a consumer, or as a professional, do I need to buy the package software that existed that solved the problem before?
zh: 如果那种原生能力直接暴露给我、你，作为一个消费者或专业人士，那我还需要买那个以前就存在、用来解决这个问题的软件包吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And is it better or worse?
zh: 它是变好了还是变差了？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think some of those categories, the market has already declared those companies dead.
zh: 我认为在某些品类里，市场已经宣判那些公司死了。

speaker: Unknown
en: In certain categories, the market is wondering, you built software 15 years ago.
zh: 在某些品类里，市场在疑惑：你十五年前做的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a new game in town called AI.
zh: 现在有个新玩家登场了，叫 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: The shape of software is going to change.
zh: 软件的形态将会改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: The market is making a judgment call whether you, your team, and your product will survive this transition to AI.
zh: 市场正在做一个判断：你、你的团队和你的产品能否在这场向 AI 的转型中活下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think all that is happening.
zh: 所以我认为这些都在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: So each company is different.
zh: 所以每家公司都不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at a fundamental level, I believe, we spent our lives building software.
zh: 而在根本层面上，我相信——我们一辈子都在造软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: It had no opinion.
zh: 它没有自己的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We bought software and it did kind of deterministic tasks.
zh: 我们买的软件做的是某种确定性的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the future, software will come with an opinion, right?
zh: 而未来，软件会带着自己的观点（opinion），对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Your AI doctor will actually have an opinion, but somebody has to train it, somebody has to give it context, and it has to learn.
zh: 你的 AI 医生会真的有自己的观点，但必须有人训练它，有人给它上下文，而它必须学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can build intelligence into our products.
zh: 我们可以把智能构建到产品里。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you build intelligence into our products, they will come with an opinion.
zh: 如果你把智能构建到产品里,它们就会带有一种观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: None of the software in the last 20 years came with an opinion.
zh: 过去 20 年里没有任何软件带有观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the entire software industry will get rewritten in the next 10 years.
zh: 所以整个软件行业将在未来 10 年被重写。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the market's making a judgment call.
zh: 而市场正在做一个判断。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which ones of these categories will survive?
zh: 这些类别中哪些会存活下来?

speaker: Unknown
en: Which of these companies will survive?
zh: 这些公司中哪些会存活下来?

speaker: Unknown
en: Possibly getting a bunch of them wrong.
zh: 可能会看错其中一大堆。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll see.
zh: 我们拭目以待。

speaker: Unknown
en: Time will tell.
zh: 时间会证明一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think the biggest question is that people are not asking right now?
zh: 你认为人们现在没有问的最大问题是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a hard question to answer.
zh: 这个问题很难回答。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I don't know what question.
zh: 比如,我不知道是什么问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know if it's a question per se.
zh: 我不确定它本身是不是一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the market is, in a way, confused.
zh: 我认为市场在某种程度上是困惑的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can see that every day.
zh: 你每天都能看到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: That, you know, some things go up rapidly for a week and suddenly they go down rapidly for a week because the market changes mind.
zh: 你知道,有些东西一周内快速上涨,然后突然又一周内快速下跌,因为市场改变了想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of the long-term trends are obvious.
zh: 一些长期趋势是显而易见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's obvious that this technology is big enough that it is going to have a long, far-reaching impact in our lifetime, so the next tens of years.
zh: 很明显,这项技术已经足够庞大,在我们有生之年,也就是未来几十年,将产生深远的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is the early days.
zh: 我认为现在还处于早期阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also clear that this technology is extremely compute consumptive than any other technology in the past.
zh: 同样明显的是,这项技术比以往任何技术都极其消耗算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to build lots more capacity around the world, and you can see that in the prices of, in the elements of what goes into building compute.
zh: 我们需要在世界各地建设更多容量,你可以从价格中看到这一点,从构建算力的各种要素中看到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see that in energy prices, you can see that in nuclear, you can see that in generators, you can see that in, you know.
zh: 你可以从能源价格中看到,你可以从核电中看到,你可以从发电机中看到,你可以从,你知道的。

speaker: Unknown
en: States saying, I don't want more data centers.
zh: 各州说,我不想要更多数据中心了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm up my eyeballs in data centers.
zh: 我已经被数据中心淹没了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're seeing all of that.
zh: 所以你看到了所有这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's clear that there's going to be huge demand going forward.
zh: 但很明显,未来将会有巨大的需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's also clear that every one of us believes that our personal AI should be able to do a lot more, and it's going to need to get better, right?
zh: 我认为同样明显的是,我们每个人都相信我们的个人 AI 应该能做更多的事情,而它需要变得更好,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure you are an avid user of some version of Claude, Gemini, or OpenAI.
zh: 我相信你是 Claude、Gemini 或 OpenAI 某个版本的忠实用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you?
zh: 你是吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I use all of them.
zh: 我全都用。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of them, right?
zh: 全都用,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Literally, Grok, OpenAI, Claude.
zh: 确切地说,Grok、OpenAI、Claude。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you use them, have you ever got yourself thinking, I wish it could do a bit more than what it just did?
zh: 当你使用它们时,你有没有想过,我希望它能比刚才做的多做一点?

speaker: Unknown
en: Every day.
zh: 每天。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I get very frustrated with them.
zh: 我对它们感到非常沮丧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're telling me this thing's not as good as it needs to be?
zh: 所以你是在告诉我这东西还没有好到它需要的程度?

speaker: Unknown
en: No, it's definitely not.
zh: 不,肯定没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which means somebody's got to have to train a lot more, get a lot more compute, get it trained, get better, right?
zh: 这意味着必须有人训练更多,获得更多算力,把它训练好,让它变好,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that means there's immense demand for capacity in the next few years.
zh: 所以这意味着未来几年容量需求巨大。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to have a lot more capacity demands on AI because we've got to train the models better, make this intelligence and get smarter.
zh: 我们对 AI 的容量需求会多得多,因为我们必须更好地训练模型,让这种智能变得更聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of us in enterprise are frustrated because it doesn't understand education.
zh: 我们企业界的很多人都很沮丧,因为它不理解教育。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're saying, why can't it be smart enough to understand?
zh: 他们说,为什么它不能聪明到能够理解?

speaker: Unknown
en: It was so smart here, why not here?
zh: 它在这里那么聪明,为什么在这里不行?

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're all waiting for it to get more capability and more capacity.
zh: 所以我们都在等待它获得更多能力和更多容量。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just think this is an unstoppable trend that's ahead of us.
zh: 我只是认为这是摆在我们面前的一个不可阻挡的趋势。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're underestimating demand across all dimensions of this, whether it's computer intelligence or what these models are capable of, which means there's going to be tons and tons of development.
zh: 我认为我们在所有维度上都低估了需求,无论是计算机智能还是这些模型的能力,这意味着将会海量的开发。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think every piece of software is going to get rewritten, every consumer application you use.
zh: 我认为每一款软件都会被重写，你用的每一个消费级应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of the applications we use on our phones, the way we're used to using them, there's a lot of UI involved, a lot of manual work involved.
zh: 我们在手机上用的很多应用，我们习惯的那种使用方式，涉及大量 UI，涉及大量手工操作。

speaker: Unknown
en: If AI is going to be so good at being an agent and using an MCP server, it's going to fix all that stuff, right?
zh: 如果 AI 在做智能体和使用 MCP server 方面会这么厉害，它会把那些东西全都修好，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's lots and lots of stuff that's going to happen that needs to get done.
zh: 所以会有大量大量的事情将要发生、需要去完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's tremendous demand.
zh: 所以需求是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The market is just going through this digestion phase of figuring out what gyrations are going to cause which thing to be overvalued or undervalued.
zh: 市场只是在经历一个消化阶段，试图弄清楚哪些波动会导致哪些东西被高估或低估。

speaker: Unknown
en: Compute is a huge topic.
zh: 算力是一个巨大的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were just interviewing Fall yesterday.
zh: 我们昨天刚采访了 Fall。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know Fall?
zh: 你认识 Fall 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Generative Media AI company.
zh: 一家生成式媒体 AI 公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: They do both compute.
zh: 他们既做算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: They also have APIs and all the other kinds of layers, but they started as compute, and then they noticed with all these video models, the voice, the 3D, like audio, all this kind of stuff that's going on.
zh: 他们也有 API 和其他各种层，但他们是从算力起家的，然后他们注意到所有这些视频模型，语音、3D，比如音频，所有这类正在进行的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those ones are really just starting.
zh: 那些才刚刚起步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's tremendous demand and those ones are gonna need more compute than anybody else.
zh: 而且需求巨大，那些会比其他任何人都需要更多算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we were talking through all the different layers of that and like all the Neo clouds that are coming out and how even with hyperscalers, I was talking to, I forget who it was, but it was at the RAISE Summit.
zh: 所以我们聊了所有不同的层，比如所有正在涌现的 Neo 云，以及即使超大规模云厂商，我在和某人聊，我忘了是谁了，但是在 RAISE Summit 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was Andrew Feldman from Cerebris and he was talking about this.
zh: 我记得是 Cerebris 的 Andrew Feldman，他在谈这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were talking to CJ at MongoDB and he was saying hyperscalers are turning away their top customers because they don't have capacity.
zh: 我们在和 MongoDB 的 CJ 聊，他说超大规模云厂商正在拒绝他们的顶级客户，因为他们没有容量。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do you think about that as a CEO in this era with everything changing around and your customers and your company and all this kind of stuff?
zh: 所以作为这个时代的 CEO，在一切都翻天覆地、你的客户、你的公司等等这些情况下，你是怎么想的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, everything you said is true.
zh: 听着，你说的都是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a constraint on compute right now because there's too much demand.
zh: 现在算力确实存在约束，因为需求太多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody needs more compute.
zh: 每个人都需要更多算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your video model friends need more compute to be able to build better videos and edit them.
zh: 你的视频模型朋友们需要更多算力才能做出更好的视频并编辑它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your ChatGPT needs more compute to be smarter, to be able to satisfy and not have you frustrated.
zh: 你的 ChatGPT 需要更多算力才能更聪明，才能让你满意而不让你沮丧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your enterprise models need more compute because we need to put more intelligence into our enterprise capabilities so we can rewrite software with opinions.
zh: 你的企业模型需要更多算力，因为我们需要把更多智能注入我们的企业能力，这样我们才能带着自己的观点重写软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's no point.
zh: 所以说没有任何一点是不成立的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way you think about it is you're in for a very long build phase in the industry.
zh: 你看待这个问题的方式是，你将进入行业里一个非常漫长的建设阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in the next 10 years, it's highly possible that 10 to 20% of our operating spend...
zh: 我认为在接下来的 10 年里，很有可能我们 10% 到 20% 的运营支出……

speaker: Unknown
en: It moves more towards technology than it already has.
zh: 会比现在更加向技术倾斜。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a huge amount of spend that's going to happen in technology.
zh: 会有巨额的支出发生在技术上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It happened in people.
zh: 过去发生在人身上。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to need more AI-ready people, so I don't buy the jobs argument.
zh: 我们将需要更多 AI 就绪的人才，所以我不认同那种关于就业岗位的论调。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have so many things to do, there's not enough people to do it.
zh: 有太多事情要做，没有足够的人去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Either it's retraining or hiring more people that go to understand the AI stuff.
zh: 要么是再培训，要么是雇更多懂 AI 的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in that process of technological upheaval, people are going to want more robust security infrastructure.
zh: 我认为在这场技术剧变的过程中，人们会想要更健壮的安全基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: So from that perspective, we know the demand is there.
zh: 所以从那个角度看，我们知道需求就在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just have to make sure we get both new products that serve that demand, and also we have to make sure that our existing products don't fall short in customers' expectations of what AI must be embedded into those products as well.
zh: 我们只需确保我们既推出服务那种需求的新产品，也要确保我们的现有产品不会在客户对「这些产品必须内嵌 AI」的期望上掉链子。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about this with your workforce?
zh: 你在员工队伍上是怎么考虑这个的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Checking on people if they're AI native?
zh: 检查员工是否是 AI 原生的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we've interviewed some CEOs that are really strict about this.
zh: 我是说，我们采访过一些在这件事上非常严格的 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very hard to check on people who are AI native.
zh: 要检查谁是不是 AI 原生其实很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not deploying little tests?
zh: 你们没有部署一些小测试吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there are two or three things you can do.
zh: 我觉得有两三件事可以做。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, what we're doing is, you know, when there is no expert, then people learn from each other.
zh: 第一，我们在做的事情是，你知道，当没有专家的时候，人们就互相学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: So twice a week, I run this meeting called AIIO.
zh: 所以每周两次，我主持一个叫 AIIO 的会。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like the old MacDoll had a form.
zh: 就像以前 MacDoll 有一个例会形式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just not AIIO, okay?
zh: 它就叫 AIIO，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: We get the top 24 technical people on a call every two days for two hours in the morning.
zh: 我们让 24 位顶级技术人员每两天开一次电话会，早上开两个小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they walk through what they're working on, how they're thinking about it, why they're doing certain things.
zh: 他们会讲他们正在做什么、他们怎么想的、为什么做某些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it suddenly gives more strength to the other 23 people to understand, oh, my God, this person is a smart engineer.
zh: 这样突然就让另外 23 个人更有力量去理解，哦天哪，这个人是位聪明的工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's how he's thinking about it.
zh: 他是这么思考这件事的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They get a chance to ask questions.
zh: 他们有机会提问。

speaker: Unknown
en: They get to learn from that person and vice versa.
zh: 他们能向那个人学习，反之亦然。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do that every twice a week so that people start understanding what's important, how do we get it.
zh: 我们每两周做两次，这样人们开始理解什么重要，我们怎么得到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: At a more micro level, it's happening in teams.
zh: 在更微观的层面上，这发生在团队里。

speaker: Unknown
en: We will take a team and say, okay, go out and take a third of your workforce and make sure you're hiring into hackathons because they're learning themselves.
zh: 我们会拿一个团队说，好，出去从你的员工里拿三分之一，确保你往黑客马拉松里招人，因为他们自己也在学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think those are the two AI native people.
zh: 我认为那些就是两种 AI 原生的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We infuse those AI native people into teams and say, keep hiring until you get to make sure that these people are more people in that team than people who've been there before.
zh: 我们把这些 AI 原生的人注入团队，并说，持续招人，直到确保这些人在那个团队里比以前就在的人更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Overwhelming these teams with more AI-native people, you start watching that you start seeing a change in behavior.
zh: 用更多 AI 原生的人淹没这些团队，你开始观察，你开始看到行为上的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Features start getting out faster.
zh: 功能开始更快地发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of the people who've been there for longer term who haven't played with AI start playing with it more.
zh: 一些待得更久、没玩过 AI 的人开始更多地玩它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then we have to create sort of a transformation.
zh: 所以那时我们得创造一种转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if enough people start being part of the transformation, I think some people who don't get it will self-select out.
zh: 如果足够多的人开始成为这场转变的一部分，我认为一些不理解的人会自我选择离开。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the approach we have.
zh: 所以这就是我们的方法。 [[562→本条为 562]]

speaker: Unknown
en: It's unlike the approach where some other people don't say, oh, I don't need a third of my people because they're not going to get it.
zh: 这不同于其他一些人的方法，他们不说，哦，我不需要三分之一的人，因为他们不会懂的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not the way to do it.
zh: 那不是做事的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: When did you start hiring from hackathons?
zh: 你是什么时候开始从黑客马拉松招人的？

speaker: Unknown
en: About, I'd say, nine months ago.
zh: 大概，我想说，九个月前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really?
zh: 真的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How'd you come up with that idea?
zh: 你是怎么想到这个主意的？

speaker: Unknown
en: How am I going to know that if you know how to use OpenClaw?
zh: 我怎么才能知道你会用 OpenClaw 呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, how am I going to know you understand what an agent is?
zh: 那，我怎么才能知道你理解什么是智能体呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're not playing with it already, you're not sitting going back home from work saying, I can't wait to get my hands on the new development that came out yesterday or use Azure Foundry or use Anthropic.
zh: 如果你还没有在玩它，你没有在下班回家的路上想着，我等不及要上手昨天发布的新东西，或者用 Azure Foundry 或者用 Anthropic。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're not going home and figuring stuff out yourself, that's a problem.
zh: 如果你不回家自己琢磨东西，那就有问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're not curious and not learning, where am I going to find these people?
zh: 如果你不好奇也不学习，我去哪里找这些人呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's pretty creative.
zh: 这挺有创意的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So before speaking with you, I spoke with Carl, who's on your board, and I asked him, like I asked many people who's around this office if they have any questions for you, anything I should ask.
zh: 所以在和你谈话之前，我和你们董事会成员 Carl 谈过，我问他，就像我问这间办公室周围的很多人一样，如果你有任何想问你的问题，有什么我应该问的。

speaker: Unknown
en: For some reason, no one in the office would answer the question besides Lee, and I'll ask that afterwards.
zh: 出于某种原因，办公室里除了 Lee 没有人愿意回答这个问题，我稍后会问那个。

en: I think two years from now, that will become less apparent.
zh: 我认为两年之后，这一点会变得不那么明显。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the market would have figured out its fair shares of failures and successes, and the market will get more discerning, which is what typically happens at that point in time in the cycle.
zh: 我认为市场会搞清楚它那份失败与成功，市场会变得更有鉴别力，而这通常是在周期中那个时间点会发生的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It usually takes five years, but we talked about compressing timelines.
zh: 这通常需要五年，但我们谈到过时间线在压缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it doesn't take away from the immense appetite for AI.
zh: 我认为这不会减损对 AI 的巨大需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't take away from the amount of reimagination and redevelopment that's going to be needed from a software perspective.
zh: 它不会减损从软件角度来看将要需要的种种重新构想和重新开发。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I think the market could go through some stumbles and bumbles over the course of the next two to five years.
zh: 但是，是的，我认为市场在未来两到五年里可能会经历一些磕磕绊绊。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my favorite questions that we ask every interview is a partner question.
zh: 我们每次采访都会问的一个我最喜欢的问题是合作伙伴问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of my partners is Brex.
zh: 我的一位合作伙伴是 Brex。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're the performance credit card.
zh: 他们是主打性能的信用卡。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're super intelligent finance.
zh: 他们是超级智能的金融。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was an investor in Brex when it had just started.
zh: 我在 Brex 刚起步的时候就是它的投资人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before the acquisition?
zh: 是在收购之前吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I was an investor at a billion-dollar valuation when they were there.
zh: 我在他们处于十亿美元估值的时候投资了他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: My daughter used to work there.
zh: 我女儿曾在那里工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: My son-in-law used to work there.
zh: 我女婿曾在那里工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: No way.
zh: 不会吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know Henrique really well, yes.
zh: 我和 Henrique 非常熟，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, amazing.
zh: 哦，太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is great.
zh: 那这真是太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is my favorite question.
zh: 这是我最喜欢的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So because they're all about performance, I like to ask people, you've had an outstanding career.
zh: 因为他们讲究的是性能，所以我喜欢问别人，你的职业生涯非常出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've learned from Larry.
zh: 你向 Larry 学过。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've learned from Masa.
zh: 你向 Masa 学过。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've learned from yourself.
zh: 你向你自己学过。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've learned from Lee.
zh: 你向 Lee 学过。

speaker: Unknown
en: You learn from everybody in this office every day.
zh: 你每天都在向这间办公室里的每个人学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'm curious if there's anybody throughout that arc that has really inspired you and kept you motivated.
zh: 但我很好奇，在这段历程中，是否有谁真正启发过你、让你保持动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I struggle to find one role model in life because every role model has certain parts of their life that you don't want to emulate, but there are certain parts you do.
zh: 我很难在人生中找到一个唯一的榜样，因为每个榜样的人生中都有某些部分是你不想效仿的，但也有某些部分是你想效仿的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you don't have to go sort of spend time with it incessantly, but you obviously get a chance to spend time.
zh: 而且我认为你不必一直不停地花时间和他们相处，但显然你有机会和他们共度时光。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, like, take Elon.
zh: 比如，拿 Elon 来说。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is not there to get inspired by him?
zh: 他有什么不值得你受到启发的呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: He built electric cars, which when people didn't think electric cars existed, he put a rocket up in space.
zh: 他造了电动车，在人们还不认为电动车存在的时候；他把火箭送上了太空。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's got things landing on Mars and Moon and things he's done.
zh: 他有东西降落在火星和月球上，还有他做过的那些事。

speaker: Unknown
en: NASA was funded for years and didn't do as well as he's doing them.
zh: NASA 资助了那么多年，做得都没他好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when he puts it, he's got Starlink.
zh: 所以当他推出的时候，他还有 Starlink。

speaker: Unknown
en: Satellites up there, we're sticking them on cars, boats, and planes to make sure that we have connectivity.
zh: 卫星挂在天上，我们把它装到汽车、船和飞机上，确保我们有网络连接。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's tons of stuff that he's done, which is so radical, which none of us have thought.
zh: 所以他做了大量极其激进的事情，是我们谁都没想过的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the principle he's sort of explained to us there is if you take a really hard problem nobody's working on, if you get it right, you win, and you win big.
zh: 我认为他在这里向我们阐释的原则是：如果你选一个没人做的真正困难的问题，做对了，你就赢了，而且是赢得很大。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look around here, a lot of entrepreneurs are busy trying to solve small problems because this is the problem they can see that far to solve the problem.
zh: 如果你看看周围，很多创业者忙着解决小问题，因为这就是他们能看得那么远、从而解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Elon cannot see when he comes up with a problem he's trying to solve.
zh: Elon 在想出一个他要解决的问题时，是看不到那么远的。

speaker: Unknown
en: He can't see that far, but he thinks if he tries to put his mind to it, that problem gets solved.
zh: 他看不到那么远，但他认为只要他用心去做，那个问题就会被解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're talking about space companies, space manufacturing, space mining, space data centers.
zh: 我们在谈论太空公司、太空制造、太空采矿、太空数据中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Shit, no, don't know where it started, right?
zh: 见鬼，不，不知道这一切是从哪开始的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But they're out there thinking about it, a bunch of people thinking about it.
zh: 但他们就在那里思考这些事，一群人在思考这些事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's inspirational.
zh: 我认为这就是鼓舞人心的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you look at Masa, you know, he's got a crazy appetite for risk.
zh: 我认为你看看 Masa，你知道，他对风险有着疯狂的胃口。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, he's taken that business which used to be SoftBank.
zh: 你知道，他拿着那门曾经是 SoftBank 的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a software bank.
zh: 它原本是一家软件银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: He used to sell software, back his software when he started his company.
zh: 他以前卖软件，在他创办公司时靠他的软件起家。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's pivoted it 20 times since then.
zh: 而从那以后他已经转型了 20 次。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's been the richest man in the world and he's become poor.
zh: 他当过世界首富，也变得一贫如洗。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was the richest man for 80-some days.
zh: 他当了八十多天的首富。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then he went back being worth nothing.
zh: 然后他变回了身无分文。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's gone back and built himself up.
zh: 他又重新把自己建设起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So these people are inspirational for different reasons, for their creativity, their innovation, their big thinking, for their relentlessness, for their persistence.
zh: 所以这些人鼓舞人心的原因各不相同，因为他们的创造力、他们的创新、他们的大格局思维、他们的不屈不挠、他们的坚持。

speaker: Unknown
en: People like Larry, there's so many people who can inspire you in different aspects of life.
zh: 像 Larry 这样的人，有那么多人在人生的不同方面都能启发你。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you just have to find the person to inspire you for the particular thing you're looking at.
zh: 所以你只需要针对你正在关注的特定事情，找到能启发你的那个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was somewhere last week, I went to a conference and Steph was on stage speaking and my son was there listening to him.
zh: 上周我在某个地方，我去参加一个大会，Steph 在台上演讲，我儿子在那里听他讲话。

speaker: Unknown
en: My son is obsessed with basketball.
zh: 我儿子痴迷篮球。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Steph talked about this next play mentality.
zh: Steph 谈到了这种“下一球心态”。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, you can't win if you can't get it as the last play that you missed.
zh: 就是说，如果你总揪着你错过的最后一球，你就赢不了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You got to focus on the next play.
zh: 你得专注于下一球。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's kind of, that's an interesting lesson whether in business or you're in sport.
zh: 无论是在商业还是在体育中，这都是一个很有意思的教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can find different people inspire you.
zh: 所以你可以找到不同的人来启发你。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you get more and more successful, how do you continue to find people that challenge you and don't just become yes men?
zh: 随着你越来越成功，你要如何继续找到能挑战你的人，而不是让他们都变成只会说“是”的人？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, I'm constantly feeling like I'm an underachiever every time I look around me.
zh: 哦，我每次环顾四周，都不断觉得自己是个成就不足的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's like young people running large hedge funds who've done so well in investing until the time they go back and reinvent themselves.
zh: 有年轻人在运营大型对冲基金，他们在投资上做得那么出色，直到他们回去重新改造自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are people who put stuff on Mars.
zh: 有人把东西送上了火星。

speaker: Unknown
en: Compared to their achievements, I'm just running a regular cybersecurity company trying to make sure that, you know, we protect the world.
zh: 和他们的成就相比，我只是在经营一家普通的网络安全公司，努力确保我们保护这个世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what comes next?
zh: 那接下来是什么呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Next comes tomorrow, and tomorrow's going to be a wonderful day.
zh: 接下来是明天，明天将会是美好的一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be beautiful.
zh: 它会很美好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to wake up really excited about the day.
zh: 我们会带着对新一天的真正兴奋醒来。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll work hard, and we go home really excited, hang out with the family.
zh: 我们会努力工作，然后带着真正的兴奋回家，和家人团聚。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there'll be day after.
zh: 然后还有后天。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the same thing?
zh: 同样的事情是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Pretty good answer.
zh: 相当好的回答。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have to.
zh: 你不必这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is if you set too many expectations on yourself, you're bound to feel disappointed.
zh: 问题在于，如果你给自己设定太多期望，你注定会感到失望。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you don't set that high an expectation, if you set an expectation of doing your best, then good things will happen.
zh: 但如果你不设定那么高的期望，如果你设定的期望是尽力而为，那么好事就会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Were you always this calm?
zh: 你一直都是这么冷静吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is my calm in terms of it's kind of the karmic calm.
zh: 这是我的冷静，可以说是业力式的冷静。

speaker: Unknown
en: The karmic calm is that you have to try to do your best.
zh: 业力式的冷静就是，你必须努力做到最好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to put your heart and soul into it.
zh: 你必须全心全意地投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to want to win.
zh: 你必须想要赢。

speaker: Unknown
en: But do you see like it's like kind of contradicting because like you're so paranoid but you're also like it'll be okay.
zh: 但你不觉得这有点矛盾吗？因为你这么偏执，但你又觉得「没事的，会好的」。

speaker: Unknown
en: Life is a series of contradictions, right?
zh: 人生就是一连串的矛盾，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the yin and the yang.
zh: 这是阴和阳。

speaker: Unknown
en: I sort of torque myself up every time and I start feeling freaked out if I fail, something doesn't work out, I'll be a mental mess and I won't be able to make anything happen.
zh: 我每次都会把自己逼得很紧，我开始感到惊慌，如果我失败了，某件事没成，我会精神崩溃，什么都做不成。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I have to work on a principle of do your best and then things will take their course.
zh: 所以我必须按照一个原则来工作：尽力而为，然后顺其自然。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it works against you, wake up in the morning, shake it off and do your best again.
zh: 如果结果对你不利，早上醒来，甩掉它，再次尽力而为。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is an explain mentality.
zh: 这是一种解释的心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get hung up on what happened yesterday, you won't be good.
zh: 你如果纠结于昨天发生的事，你就不会好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't be somebody else because if you be somebody else then you lose all the other things that are you about you.
zh: 你不能成为别人，因为如果你成为别人，你就会失去属于你自己的所有其他东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, you can be all the things I said from a go get shit done, be paranoid because you want to win.
zh: 是的，你可以同时具备我说的所有特质——把事情搞定、保持偏执，因为你想要赢。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the same time, you have to have some degree of inner calm to be able to deal with the moves, the pressures, everything of the job.
zh: 同时，你必须有一定程度的内心平静，才能应对这份工作的各种变动、压力和一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: No AI psychosis over here, I guess.
zh: 我想这里没有什么 AI 精神病。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no AI psychosis.
zh: 没有 AI 精神病。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think that's a great, positive, optimistic way and place to end it.
zh: 好吧，我认为这是一个非常棒、积极、乐观的方式来结束这期节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nikesh, thank you so much for taking the time, letting us rearrange your office.
zh: Nikesh，非常感谢你抽出时间，让我们重新布置了你的办公室。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for coming all the way here.
zh: 谢谢你们大老远跑来这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: We appreciate that.
zh: 我们很感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: My pleasure.
zh: 我的荣幸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

en: Hey, it's Molly.
zh: 嘿，我是 Molly。

zh: 如果你喜欢我们的访谈，请看看我们的通讯 sorcery.vc，我们每周发送一封顶级交易和科技头条的邮件，还会对我们的播客访谈做更深入的展开。
